'''Saba Valadkhan''' ({{langx|fa|صبا ولدخان}}) is an [[Iranian American]] [[biomedical scientist]], and an Assistant Professor and [[RNA]] researcher at [[Case Western Reserve University]] in [[Cleveland]], Ohio.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-05-06|title=Saba Valadkhan|url=https://case.edu/cancer/members/member-directory/saba-valadkhan|access-date=2020-07-12|website=Case Comprehensive Cancer Center {{!}} School of Medicine {{!}} Case Western Reserve University|language=en}}</ref> In 2005, she was awarded the [[GE]] / ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' Young Scientist Award for her breakthrough in understanding the mechanism of [[spliceosome]]s - "akin to finding the Holy Grail of the [[Splicing (genetics)|splicing]] [[catalysis]] field" <ref name=":1">{{cite web|url=http://www.payvand.com/news/05/aug/1088.html|title=Saba Valadkhan of Case Western Reserve University Wins Young Scientist Award|website=www.payvand.com|access-date=2005-08-12|archive-date=2021-01-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210126015044/http://www.payvand.com/news/05/aug/1088.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> - a critical area of research, given that "20 percent or 30 percent of all human genetic diseases are caused by mistakes that the spliceosome makes".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aaas.org/news/releases/2005/0210ys-Valadkhan.shtml|title=News|website=aaas.org|access-date=2005-08-12|archive-date=2008-06-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080620211459/http://www.aaas.org/news/releases/2005/0210ys-Valadkhan.shtml|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Education ==
Valadkhan qualified as a medical doctor at [[Tehran University of Medical Sciences|Tehran University of Medial Sciences]] in [[Iran]] in 1996. She moved to the United States to pursue her Ph.D. at [[Columbia University]], in New York City.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Dr. Saba Valadkhan: A Renowned Biomedical Scientist|url=http://www.payvand.com/news/08/dec/1282.html|access-date=2020-07-12|website=www.payvand.com|archive-date=2020-11-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201130045142/http://www.payvand.com/news/08/dec/1282.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2004, she joined [[Case Western Reserve University]] in [[Cleveland]], Ohio as an Assistant Professor.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Valadkhan Lab|url=http://www.valadkhanlab.org/news.php|access-date=2020-07-12|website=www.valadkhanlab.org}}</ref>

== Doctoral research ==
Valadkhan studied the role of [[small nuclear RNA]]s in the human[[ spliceosome]] under the supervision of Prof. [[James L. Manley]].<ref name=":1" /> The main focus of her research is elucidating the structure and function of the [[catalytic core]] of the spliceosome by taking advantage of a novel, minimal spliceosome she developed. This minimal system, which consists of only two spliceosomal [[snRNA]]s, catalyzes a reaction identical to the splicing reaction. In addition to providing direct evidence for [[RNA]] [[catalysis]] in the spliceosome, and thus, settling the longstanding and central question of the identity of the [[catalytic domain]], the minimal system provides a novel and powerful tool for studying the structure and function of the spliceosome.

== Awards and honours ==
Valadkhan was presented with the Harold Weintraub award from the [[Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center]] in [[Seattle]], Washington for her doctoral thesis.<ref name=":0" /> She was named a [[Searle Scholars Program|Searle Scholar]] in 2004. She was also awarded the [[American Association for Advancement of Science]] (AAAS) Young Scientist Grand Prize in the same year.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Saba Valadkhan of Case Western Reserve University Wins Young Scientist Award|url=http://www.payvand.com/news/05/aug/1088.html|access-date=2021-09-25|website=www.payvand.com|archive-date=2021-01-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210126015044/http://www.payvand.com/news/05/aug/1088.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2006, she became a founding member of the [[Rosalind Franklin]] Society.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Home|url=https://www.rosalindfranklinsociety.org/|access-date=2020-07-12|website=www.rosalindfranklinsociety.org}}</ref> She was also honoured with the Nsoroma Award from Cleveland Chapter of the National Technical Association in 2006.
